domain: Disaster Anthropology / Commitment Systems / Temporal Institutional Analysis
topic_summary: Analysis of the Aneyoshi tsunami stone's 'do not build below this line' directive across 78 years of non-catastrophe (1933-2011), examining whether the kernel decayed to commemorative symbol or retained behavioral force. The 2011 Tōhoku tsunami provided a D5 catastrophe-theorem test: Aneyoshi village survived while neighboring settlements were destroyed, suggesting the commitment remained operationally live.

key_entities: Aneyoshi tsunami stone (1933 memorial marker with land-use prohibition)
Aneyoshi village (settlement that observed the stone's directive)
Neighboring coastal settlements (communities that built below equivalent elevation lines)
key_tensions: Commemorative-husk interpretation vs behavioral-competence interpretation of the stone's function across 78 years

axes.structural_delta: Stone as dead symbol: commitment decayed to ritual observance without behavioral constraint
axes.primary_observable: Land-use pattern divergence from stone directive; memorial tourism vs functional compliance
axes.selection_reason: First reading of contested kernel; represents decay hypothesis

axes.structural_delta: Stone as live constraint: commitment retained operational force in land-use decisions
axes.primary_observable: Actual building locations relative to stone line; survival differential in 2011
axes.selection_reason: Second reading of contested kernel; represents retention hypothesis

axes.structural_delta: Rate of commitment erosion across generations absent catastrophe reinforcement
axes.primary_observable: Generational distance from 1933 event; land-use compliance by cohort age
axes.selection_reason: Independent axis: measures temporal mechanism affecting kernel viability; distinct observable from kernel readings

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Neighboring settlements' land-use decisions as control group
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Captured as observable within behavioral_competence_reading; not structurally independent

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Wave height and inundation physics at stone elevation
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Physical constraint underlying both readings; not a distinct axis of commitment analysis

omegas.description: Were there partial violations (building slightly below stone line) that went unpunished pre-2011? Intermediate states between full decay and full retention may exist.
What enforced the directive if behavioral_competence reading is correct? Social sanction, legal prohibition, or internalized norm? Mechanism unspecified in kernel contest.
Did 2011 survival reset the decay clock? If so, the kernel may now be in a different phase of its lifecycle than the 78-year period tested.
Does the stone's function depend on literacy and historical knowledge transmission? If so, the commitment is not purely behavioral but requires cultural infrastructure.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel contest is well-defined with decisive empirical test (2011 tsunami). Temporal_decay_gradient passes independence test as distinct mechanism axis.

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The directive 'do not build below this stone line' inscribed on the 1933 Aneyoshi tsunami memorial, stabilizing a land-use prohibition grounded in catastrophe memory
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Authority derives from catastrophe witness testimony (1933 survivors) encoded in stone; legitimacy grounded in demonstrated predictive validity (2011 survival)

readings.commitment: Stone as memorial artifact: commitment decayed to symbolic observance without behavioral constraint on land use
readings.expected_structural_delta: High epsilon: land-use decisions made independently of stone directive; survival in 2011 attributed to luck or other factors; stone functions as museum piece

readings.commitment: Stone as live land-use rule: commitment retained operational force in building location decisions across 78 years
readings.authority_grounding: Catastrophe memory / demonstrated predictive validity / internalized norm
readings.expected_structural_delta: Very low epsilon: land-use decisions constrained by stone directive; 2011 survival causally linked to compliance; stone functions as active regulatory mechanism

axiom_contradictions.basis: No single framework can hold both 'the commitment decayed to non-functional symbol' and 'the commitment retained operational constraint force' as simultaneously true for the same 78-year period. The 2011 survival outcome provides decisive evidence for one reading or the other.
